messages:
samir.khan: Quick check-in on StratusHealth postmortem action items — can owners confirm status? TL;DR: VPC peering route flap, on-prem NAT session limit, and the isolation bug fix is in canary. Need owners, ETA, blockers. :wave:
elaine.wu: I own the VPC peering follow-up. Today: validated peering AWS<>customer edge config, found BGP hold-timer mismatch. Plan: push config change to staging peering tomorrow, then 24h monitor. ETA: 48h. :white_check_mark:
pratik.rao: On NAT limit — confirmed customer's on-prem firewall had session limit reached during deduped bursts. Ops flagged concurrent connections spike from our telemetry. Working with customer NOC to increase session table, also prepping a fallback policy on our side to reduce concurrent flows. ETA: 3 days pending NOC approval.
ivy_m: Isolation bug (tenant traffic cross-talk) — fix merged to master yesterday, canary rollout started this morning on 10% of Dedicated nodes. Observability hooks added to trace headers. Early metrics look clean. Will expand to 50% if no regressions in 6h.
ops-bot: deploy: canary rollout for isolation-fix v1.2.3 started by ivy_m at 2174000300. Links: https://console.redwood/rollouts/2174/isolation-fix
matt_l: Heads-up — customer reported config drift from their side during last peering event. Suggest adding a short pre-check in our onboarding checklist to validate vendor firmware compat. Also could help reduce recurrence.
samir.khan: Agree on checklist addition. Pratik + Elaine, can you coordinate on a small runbook entry? I'd like a single doc we can link in customer onboarding and in incident triage. Minimal scope: what to check, commands, expected outputs, contact escalation matrix.
elaine.wu: I'll draft the peering pre-check section. Will add BGP hold-timer, AS path, and route-map sanity checks. ETA: EOD tomorrow.
pratik.rao: I'll draft the NAT/session mitigation steps and the fallback rate-limiter snippet. Putting together a small iptables-ish example and our side rate-limit pseudo-config. ETA: 48 hours.
ivy_m: I'll update the postmortem with canary metrics and link to traces once 24h lookback is available. If canary is green at 50% expand, I'll mark bug as resolved and update the incident status.
samir.khan: Two pattern items I want to capture for the recurring-incident registry: 1) customer-side firmware-induced BGP flaps after scheduled updates, 2) spikes in concurrent connections when our batching changes coincide with customer bulk jobs. Can we tag both in the incident and add owners?
matt_l: I'll add tags and create a short entry in the recurring-incident doc. Assigning pattern-1 to network-eng, pattern-2 to infra-performance.
ops-bot: reminder: weekly incident follow-up sync tomorrow 09:30 PT. Please add updates in the doc before then.
elaine.wu: added initial draft to the runbook: https://docs.redwood/internal/onboarding/peering-precheck (will flesh after review).
pratik.rao: pasted fallback snippet here for quick review:
```
# pseudo-config for request rate limiting fallback
route-policy: if sessions>80% then reduce-burst->20%
connection-backoff: 200ms
```
ivy_m: Quick note — telemetry span for tenant-id has been added to the canary so we can detect any cross-tenant signals immediately. If anyone needs access to traces ping me.
samir.khan: OK. Owners + ETAs: Elaine (peering pre-check doc, 48h), Pratik (NAT mitigation + fallback snippet, 72h), Ivy (canary metrics + final status, 24–48h). Matt will catalog recurring patterns. If no objections I'll close the incident action list and move remaining items into the weekly follow-up board. :thumbsup:
elaine.wu: no objections, will sync with pratik on overlap points.
pratik.rao: will coordinate with customer NOC today.
ivy_m: will post canary status update in this thread once we hit 24h.
samir.khan: Thanks all. If anything blocks NOC approvals escalate to me and @matt_l.
matt_l: ack.
notes: customer: StratusHealth; affected: Dedicated cluster-42; root_causes: BGP hold timer mismatch, on-prem NAT session limit, software isolation bug; severity: P2
